title: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs
abstract: arXiv:2611.16540v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. translated_title: 基于动态情景的多资产ETF投资组合优化
translated_abstract: 投资组合的结果可能既取决于收益的建模方式，也同样取决于交易限制。针对30只在美国上市的交易所交易基金（ETF），我们比较了历史滑动窗口收益与由ARMA-GARCH模型及Student-t连接函数（copula）生成的条件情景。在946个交易日内，我们在纯做多以及有限的做多-做空约束下，评估了相互匹配的均值-方差组合与条件风险价值（CVaR）组合。在大多数比较中，历史组合表现出更高的观测风险收益比，但经过多重检验校正后，没有任何配对差异仍然显著。条件情景并未能持续降低实际发生的下行风险。我们区分了目标权重的变化与市场变动后为重新平衡持仓所需执行的交易。在所检验的测试中，放宽目标调整限制对敞口、换手率及部分收益的影响，大于改变情景数量或随机种子所带来的影响。这些发现表明，对条件情景的评估……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文比较了历史滑动窗口收益与ARMA-GARCH加Student-t Copula条件情景在30只美国ETF组合优化中的表现，发现交易限制（尤其是目标调整限制）对组合结果的影响大于情景生成方式的选择，且两种方法的表现差异经多重检验校正后均不显著。
en_tdlr: This study compares historical moving-window returns with ARMA-GARCH and Student-t copula conditional scenarios for optimizing 30 U.S.-listed ETF portfolios, finding that trading restrictions—especially the target-adjustment limit—affect portfolio outcomes more than how scenarios are generated, with no performance differences remaining significant after multiple-testing adjustment.
